prompt: Close-up of thick kale-and-potato stew in a plain white deep plate, filling 80% of a square frame. Soft, collapsed broad kale ribbons are very dark olive-green, almost black-green, with crinkled edges and light oily sheen. Soft pale-yellow 3 cm potato chunks have moist, rough edges; some are crushed into glossy, thick, spoonable beige-brown liquor with tiny translucent onion flecks. Smoked cured pork loin appears as irregular 2 cm cubes with golden-brown seared patches and juicy rosy-beige interiors. On top lies a plump, curved sausage in a lightly glossy greyish-tan natural casing, cut open to show its very coarse, moist pale beige-pink filling with visible fat and oat grains. A little steam, clean rim, no garnish or props. Camera 45° above, 85 mm, f/5.6, warm soft natural side light, sharp textures, softly blurred table edge, true-to-life colour, magazine food photo.

visible_ingredients.real_life_appearance: Braised until tender: very dark olive green, almost black-green, soft and collapsed broad ribbons about 3–5 cm long, with crinkled, curled leaf edges and a light oily sheen. Numerous tangled ribbons per portion form the bulk of the stew; they are neither bright green nor crisp and retain frilly kale edges rather than looking like smooth cabbage strips.

Simmered, not browned: soft pale-yellow to creamy-ivory chunks, roughly 3 cm, with moist, slightly crumbly flesh and rounded, rough or frayed edges. About 5–7 chunks per portion; several are partly crushed, their fluffy interiors breaking into and thickening the cooking liquor.

The original fine dice, about 0.3 cm, are now very soft and mostly integrated into the liquor. Numerous tiny translucent pale golden-beige flecks remain visible per portion, with no raw white crunch and no separately browned onion slices.

Smoked cured pork loin, seared and then braised: irregular cubes about 2 cm, roughly 12–15 per portion, some partly buried. The exterior is muted beige-brown with patchy golden-brown seared sides; exposed interiors are juicy rosy beige-pink with a firm, fine meat grain, not the smooth, uniformly pink surface of boiled ham.

One plump, gently curved sausage per portion, about 12–15 cm long and 3 cm thick, gently simmered whole and left unburst. Its natural casing is greyish-tan to light brown, lightly glossy and slightly wrinkled, without seared patches. A cut end reveals a very coarse, loose, moist pale beige-pink filling with visible pork pieces, off-white fat and pale oat or groats grains; it is not a smooth, uniform frankfurter.

Reduced and bound with crushed potato into a thick, spoonable, glossy beige-brown cooking liquor. It lightly coats the kale and meat and pools only shallowly between the ingredients, with tiny onion and potato flecks; it is neither clear nor a thin, soupy broth.
